captions.instagram:
How do the lungs work?

You breathe about 20,000 times a day without thinking. Follow one breath from your nose to 480 million tiny air sacs, and watch oxygen slip into your blood.

→ Every breath travels from your nose, down the windpipe, into two lungs.
→ Inside, the airways branch about 23 times, ending in 480 million tiny air sacs.
→ The diaphragm flattens, the chest grows, pressure drops, and air rushes in: Boyle’s law.
→ Oxygen diffuses into the blood across a wall just half a micrometre thick.
→ Each haemoglobin molecule grabs four oxygen molecules. That turns blood bright red.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/lungsclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do the lungs work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
You breathe about 20,000 times a day without thinking. Follow one breath from your nose to 480 million tiny air sacs, and watch oxygen slip into your blood.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/lungsclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/lungsclear

In this video:
• A tree of air. Air flows through your nose, throat and voice box into the windpipe, which splits into two bronchi.
• Breathing is Boyle's law. Your lungs have no muscles.
• Swapping gases by diffusion. Each alveolus is wrapped in capillaries, separated from the air by a wall about 0.5 micrometres thick.
• Haemoglobin does the carrying. Each haemoglobin molecule holds four oxygen molecules, and its S-shaped binding curve fills blood to about 98% in the lungs.
• How much air you hold. A quiet breath is about 500 mL.
• Keeping lungs clean. Mucus traps dirt and cilia sweep it up to your throat.
